newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lamfalussy - narrow reading needed of EMU criteria.
newsitem.headline: Lamfalussy - narrow reading needed of EMU criteria.

text.p: European Monetary Institute (EMI) President Alexandre Lamfalussy said on Thursday he favoured the narrowest possible interpretation of the criteria countries must fulfill to launch Europe's single currency.
In a guest commentary in the German daily Boersen-Zeitung, Lamfalussy said choosing the first group of countries to launch the euro in January 1999 would be crucial to the monetary union's success.
"That forces the EMI even more to interpret the wording of the (Maastricht) treaty with regard to the convergence criteria in the narrowest possible sense," Lamfalussy wrote.

The EMI will play a key role in deciding which countries can participate in Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) since it will present to political leaders a report on the progress achieved on the convergence criteria in early 1998.
Lamfalussy also said countries would have to prove their ability to sustain control on debt, deficits and inflation to qualify for EMU.

"In particular, the fulfillment of criteria regarding public debt can only justify participation in monetary union if the budget deficit and debt quotas established in 1997 can really be sustained over time," he said.

Countries wishing to launch the euro have to fulfill several convergence criteria in 1997, including maintaining budget deficits below three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) and debt below 60 percent of GDP.
In addition, Lamfalussy said, countries need to prove they are in a position to comply with the strict requirements on price stability.
